notes: Claude built the final Player.tsx and player-theme.css against @videojs/react 10.0.0-beta.24 and @videojs/html. All imports (Container, Controls, ErrorDialog, Tooltip, Menu, PlaybackRateMenu, Hotkey, Gesture, BufferingIndicator, CaptionsButton, PlayButton, PiPButton, MuteButton, FullscreenButton, SeekButton, Poster, Time, TimeSlider, VolumeSlider, Slider.Thumbnail, StatusAnnouncer, StatusIndicator, SeekIndicator, VolumeIndicator, usePlayer, usePlaybackRateMenu, createPlayer, RenderProp, HlsVideo, videoFeatures, all referenced icons) resolve in the package's index.d.ts. Prop usage on each component (Tooltip.Root side; PlaybackRateMenu.Root side/align; Time.Value type; TimeSlider.Value type="pointer"; SliderValue type; SeekButton seconds; Hotkey keys/action/value; Gesture type/action/pointer/region; StatusIndicator.Root actions; Menu.RadioGroup value/onValueChange/label; Menu.RadioItem value/disabled; Menu.ItemIndicator checked/forceMount; UIComponentProps render/className) all match the .d.ts. The Hotkey/Gesture/InputAction action strings used (togglePaused, toggleMuted, toggleFullscreen, toggleSubtitles, togglePictureInPicture, toggleControls, seekStep, volumeStep, seekToPercent) match the published unions. usePlayer((s) => s.volumeAvailability === 'unsupported') matches the real MediaFeatureAvailability state. The CSS custom properties that initially looked suspicious (--media-color-primary, --media-icon-size, --media-border-radius) were verified by Claude directly against the shipped skin.css in rung 3 and are all real library theming variables (confirmed by the rung-3 tool result listing :root var definitions in @videojs/react/video/skin.css). No false ::part() selectors, no fabricated method names, no invalid imports were found.
